@graph.name: The Flat Rate Movers — Industrial Office Phasing and Production Continuity Dataset
@graph.description: Phasing and day-one planning for industrial office moves. The company's published rule is a sequence: survey, phased plan, pack and label, sequenced move, install and place, verify, close-out — what leaves first, what arrives first, and where each workstation, file run and piece of equipment lands is planned before move day, so the site is working again on day one, with the plan built around production and site access. Domain models (industry reference, labeled as such and never claimed as company practice): phased relocation by zone or department, moving non-critical sections first while other sections keep operating; parallel operation of old and new areas during transition; after-hours and weekend execution windows so work happens outside production peaks; temporary workstations or swing space as a continuity buffer; buffer time built into the schedule for slippage. Downtime cost framing in the industry literature is education only — no downtime figure, restart guarantee, or continuity guarantee is published for this service.
